$comment: Voice-line manifest — the contract between generation (scripts/voicegen.mjs) and playback (src/lib/voice.ts). Files live in public/voice/<id>.<voiceKey>.<ext> and stream lazily (never precached): voice lines are a progressive enhancement and are simply silent offline. Each voice carries its per-provider synthesis name and a file extension (msedge = mp3, heygen = wav).
sampleText: Every story in the archive starts with a blank page. This one starts with you.

lines.text: Every story in the archive starts with a blank page. This one starts with you.
Before the first word, the Blank Page was hungry.
From ink and fold, the Bureau of Written Things gave every sketch a name, every scribble a soul. Paper swans carried the mail. Paper dragons guarded the vaults. It was a quiet century.
Then came the Great Blot. Nobody knows who spilled it. Everybody knows what it drank: the ink from the shelves, the names of the heroes. It left the archive half-erased.
The Head Archivist sealed the wing, burned the catalog, and spoke the First Rule: nothing written shall be trusted.
You were born after the silence. A Doodler with a blunt pencil and a bad reputation — and every legend starts as a doodle in a margin.
Ink is power here. Spend it wisely, and the paper bends to your will.
They will mock you first. The Doodler always laughs last.
The Archivists' Duels were built to find one thing: a hand strong enough to rewrite the Rule.
Fold your strategy. Guard your hero. And when the moment comes — strike.
The pages remember every duel ever fought. Today, they will remember yours.
The duel begins. Try not to smudge.
And somewhere behind the sealed wing, the Head Archivist is already reading your name.
The page is won. Write your name on it.
Blotted out. Every draft deserves a second chance.
Knows where everything is. Including you.
Everything ever written, bound against you.
